records.people: Awad Abdel Magied Aburiesh (Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Bank of Sudan, July 1971 - October 1972; Deputy Governor 1969)
records.move: from Governor and Chairman of the Board of the Bank of Sudan (July 1971 - October 1972) to a business of his own, 'Awad Abdel Magied and Partners Ltd.', set up in 1973; he had earlier joined Barclays Bank in London in 1960 as a local director before entering the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Sudan
records.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan's own career page for Aburiesh records that he joined Barclays Bank in London in 1960 as a local director before entering the Ministry of Finance and then the Bank of Sudan, and that after leaving the governorship in October 1972 he 'Set up his own private Business "Awad Abdel Magied and Partners Ltd."' in 1973. The private financial side of this career is the Barclays Bank post, which the page states plainly; the business he set up afterwards is called private by the bank's own page but its sector is not given, so it is not what the counting rests on. The same page describes Bank of Khartoum as 'Ex Barclays Bank ) after Nationalization', so the Barclays employment preceded its being taken into state hands.
records.source_title: Central Bank of Sudan - Governors of CBOS: Awad Abdel Magied Aburiesh

records.people: Ismail El-Misbah Mekki (Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Central Bank of Sudan, 1985-1989)
records.move: from Founder and Managing Director of the Islamic Bank for Western Sudan (1983-1984) and Managing Director of Fordan Commercial Co. (1984-1985) to Governor and Chairman of the Board of the Central Bank of Sudan (1985-1989)
records.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan's own career page for Mekki lists, immediately before the governorship, 'Founder & Managing Director Islamic bank for Western Sudan (Commercial Bank), 1983 - 1984' and 'Managing Director Fordan Commercial Co., 1984 - 1985'. The private side is the bank he himself founded, which the central bank's page labels a commercial bank; founding and running it is an ownership-side role, not a state posting, while his earlier career was in the Ministry of Finance and at the World Bank and IMF.
records.source_title: Central Bank of Sudan - Governors of CBOS: Ismail El-Misbah Mekki

records.people: Faroug Ibrahim Elmagbool (Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Central Bank of Sudan, 1983-1985)
records.move: from Governor and Chairman of the Board of the Central Bank of Sudan (1983-1985) to General Manager of the Sudanese French Bank (1993-1995), by way of consultancy at Almagboul Institution from 1986
records.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan's own career page for Elmagbool records him as Governor and Chairman 1983-1985 and then 'General Manager, Sudanese French Bank, 1993 - 1995', with consultancy at Almagboul Institution from 1986 in between. Filed as a public move because nothing is settled on the private side: the page names the Sudanese French Bank and Almagboul Institution without saying who owns either, and Sudanese banks of that period were variously nationalised and reprivatised, so the ownership of the receiving employer is unstated and this record is not counted as private finance.
records.source_title: Central Bank of Sudan - Governors of CBOS: Faroug Ibrahim Elmagbool

records.people: Abdelateef Hassan (Governor and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Central Bank of Sudan, 1970-1971; Chief Accountant of the bank, 1967)
records.move: from Governor and Chairman of the Board of the Central Bank of Sudan (1970-1971) to partner in the accountancy firm Abd-Altaif Eltayeb and Partners from 1971, and to a managership at KPMG's Sudan practice, auditing and advising companies and banks in Sudan
records.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan's own career page for Abdelateef Hassan records him as Governor and Chairman 1970-1971 and, under 'Other', 'Partner, Abd-Altaif Eltayeb and Partners, 1971 upto now', 'Manager, KPMG Co., Sudan' and 'Auditor and Advisor to a number of companies and banks in Sudan'. Filed as a public move because the ownership of neither employer is stated on the page: the partnership's and KPMG Sudan's ownership is left unsettled, and the KPMG managership carries no dates at all, so nothing here is counted as a move into stated private finance even though both are plainly outside the state.
records.source_title: Central Bank of Sudan - Governors of CBOS: Abdelateef Hassan

records.people: Norman T. L. Chan (Deputy Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority 1996-2005; Chief Executive of the HKMA from 1 October 2009)
records.move: from Deputy Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (1996-2005) to Vice Chairman, Asia of Standard Chartered Bank (December 2005 - June 2007), then back into government as Director of the Chief Executive's Office (2007-2009) and on to the top of the HKMA from October 2009
records.summary: Chan's official conference biography states 'From December 2005 to June 2007, Mr Chan was Vice Chairman, Asia of Standard Chartered Bank', directly after nine years as the HKMA's Deputy Chief Executive and two years before he returned as its Chief Executive. The private side is Standard Chartered Bank, a commercial banking group held by its shareholders with no state owner, named by the source; this is a different person and a different firm from the Joseph Yam / UBS record the map already holds for Hong Kong.
records.source_title: Mr Norman T L Chan, SBS, JP - speaker biography, Asian Financial Forum conference papers (Hong Kong Trade Development Council)
records.quote: From December 2005 to June 2007, Mr Chan was Vice Chairman, Asia of Standard Chartered Bank.

records.people: Gunnar Jakobsson (Deputy Governor for Financial Stability, Central Bank of Iceland, appointed 23 December 2019)
records.move: from nineteen years at the investment bank Goldman Sachs - in New York from summer 2000 and in London from 2018, latterly managing director for liquidity risk and data protection at Goldman Sachs International - to Deputy Governor for Financial Stability of the Central Bank of Iceland
records.summary: The Icelandic Prime Minister's Office announcement of his appointment sets out his whole career and states that he began work at the investment bank Goldman Sachs & Co. in the summer of 2000 and was still there, holding operational-risk, market-risk and liquidity-risk management posts through 2018 and then serving as managing director for liquidity and data protection at Goldman Sachs International in London. The private side is Goldman Sachs, which the source itself calls an investment bank and which has no state owner; the map's existing Iceland record is a different person coming out of Kaupthing Bank.
records.source_title: Gunnar Jakobsson skipadur varasedlabankastjori fjarmalastodugleika - Stjornarradid (Prime Minister's Office), 23 December 2019

records.people: Antoine Seeyave (Director on the Board of the Bank of Mauritius, appointed March 2020)
records.move: sits on the Board of the Bank of Mauritius while holding an independent directorship of JP Morgan Indian Investment Company (Mauritius) Ltd, and while chairing Happy World Ltd, which the central bank's own biography of him calls a private family-controlled company, having co-founded Innodis Ltd (1973-1998) and Floreal Knitwear Ltd
records.summary: The Bank of Mauritius publishes an individual biodata sheet for each board member. Seeyave's states he was appointed to its Board of Directors in March 2020 and holds an independent directorship of JP Morgan Indian Investment Company (Mauritius) Ltd, which is the financial employer this row turns on. The same sheet describes Happy World Ltd, which he chairs, as a private family-controlled company, and records that he co-founded Innodis Ltd from its inception in 1973 to 1998 and Floreal Knitwear Ltd; those three are private but are trading, food and textile businesses rather than finance, so they are not what counts here. The map's existing Mauritius record is a different person, Rama Krishna Sithanen.
records.source_title: Biodata - Antoine Seeyave, Board of the Bank of Mauritius

records.people: Walter C. Wassmer (member of the Monetary Board of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, appointed July 2024)
records.move: from twenty-five years at BDO Unibank, Inc. - Senior Executive Vice President and Institutional Banking Group Head from 1997 to 2022, then consultant and non-executive director from 2022 - to a seat on the Monetary Board of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, after earlier posts at Far East Bank and Trust Co. (1986-1997), Union Bank of the Philippines (1983-1986) and Bancom Finance Corporation (1980-1982)
records.summary: The Presidential Communications Office release announcing his appointment to the Monetary Board of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas lists his career post by post, including 'Senior EVP and Institutional Banking Group Head' at BDO Unibank, Inc. from 1997 to 2022 and consultant and non-executive director there from 2022. The private side is BDO Unibank, Inc. (the Philippine bank, not the BDO audit network the map carries elsewhere), whose own shareholder-structure page names its holders as SM Investments Corp. at 38.98 per cent, Sybase Equity Investments Corporation at 12.81 per cent and Multi-Realty Development Corporation at 5.95 per cent with the remainder through nominee accounts and no state holding - https://bdo.com.ph/node/22835 . The map's existing Philippine record is Rafael Buenaventura out of Philippine Commercial Industrial Bank, a different person and a different decade. He was reappointed to the Monetary Board in July 2026 for a term running to July 2032.
records.source_title: President Marcos appoints banker Walter Wassmer to BSP Monetary Board - Presidential Communications Office news release

records.people: Jakub Seidler (Czech National Bank staff 2008 to about 2014, head of its Macroprudential Policy Unit; member of the CNB Bank Board from 1 December 2024)
records.move: from six years on the Czech National Bank's staff into private banking as Chief Economist for the Czech Republic at ING Bank (2014-2021), then Chief Economist of the Czech Banking Association (mid-2021 to December 2024), and back into the central bank as a member of its Bank Board from 1 December 2024
records.summary: The Czech National Bank's own biography of its board member states 'From 2014 to 2021, he served as Chief Economist for the Czech Republic at ING Bank', between six years on the CNB's own staff and his appointment to the Bank Board for a six-year term starting on 1 December 2024, with the chief economist post at the Czech Banking Association in between. The private side is ING Bank, a commercial banking group owned by its shareholders with no state owner, and the Czech Banking Association, a trade body of commercial banks; the CNB page itself makes no ownership statement about either, so that reading of ING rests on the bank being a listed commercial group rather than on the source's words. The map's existing Czech record is Ales Michl, a different person.
records.source_title: Jakub Seidler - CNB Board Member, Czech National Bank
records.quote: From 2014 to 2021, he served as Chief Economist for the Czech Republic at ING Bank.

blanks.note: Vein closed on this document. Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago media release on the appointment of Dr Sandra Sookram as Deputy Governor for a five-year term effective 13 July 2015 (central-bank.org.tt/sites/default/files/latest-news/Media Release - Deputy Gov.pdf) read in full: the only prior employer it names is the Sir Arthur Lewis Institute of Social and Economic Studies at the University of the West Indies, St Augustine, where she was a Fellow, Academic Coordinator and acting Director. A public university is a public employer, so this appointment is no career move into or out of private finance, and no private firm is named anywhere in the release. The board-profile pages of the bank were not reached.

Confirmed blank on two of the six governor career pages read. Central Bank of Sudan 'Governors of CBOS' pages node/622 (Mahdi Elfaky Elshaikh, Governor 1988-1990) names only the Sudan Guar Company (General Manager 1993-1999) and the Gum Arabic Company Ltd (Deputy General Manager 1978-1980) outside the state, neither of them finance and neither with any ownership stated, so it is refused rather than filed. node/623 (Dr Sabir Mohammed Hassan, Governor 1993-1996 and from 1998) names only the IMF, the Ministry of Finance, universities and the Bank of Sudan itself - every employer public. Pages node/617, 618, 620 and 621 produced the four Sudan records above; node/619, 624 and 625 are the pages the map's existing Sudan records already rest on and were not re-read.

Refused, one candidate. Bank of Mauritius biodata sheet for board member Christine Sauzier (bom.mu/sites/default/files/pdf/About/cv/biodata_christine_sauzier_board_of_the_bank_of_mauritius.pdf), appointed to the Board in March 2020, read in full: it names her as Group General Counsel of CIEL Group and an Attorney-at-Law of more than 25 years, with undated directorships in health, property, finance and agro industry. No dates for the CIEL role and no statement of CIEL's ownership, so unstated ownership settles nothing and it was not filed. The bank publishes one such sheet per board member and per former managing director (Ramsahye, Toorbuth, Gaya, Tacouri, Gujadhur, Basant Roi) - these were not opened and are a cheap seam for a later round.

Confirmed blank on one document. Komercni banka's own supervisory-board CV booklet 'DR zivotopisy aj' (kb.cz/getmedia/a2435646-4f54-4d45-beb4-cc5c7c8b7a69/DR-zivotopisy-aj.pdf), downloaded and grepped in full for 'Czech National Bank', 'CNB' and 'National Bank': the booklet covers employee-elected supervisory board members (Ondrej Kudrna, Sylva Kynychova and others) and names no Czech National Bank officer at all. The hiring-firm route into Czechia via Komercni banka is closed on that document; the CNB's own bank-board biographies worked instead and the other six current board members' pages were not opened.

Not reached, one route. The Central Bank of Iceland's own news page for the appointment (cb.is/news-and-publications/article/2019-12-27-Gunnar-Jakobsson-appointed-Deputy-Governor-for-Financial-Stability) is a JavaScript application shell: curl returns a 6,471-byte loader with no text and WebFetch returns nothing readable. The record above therefore rests on the Prime Minister's Office announcement of the same appointment instead. Anyone re-checking the bank's own wording will need a rendering browser.

Mutch, Christine Charbonneau, Marjolaine Giasson, Shelley Williams, Maureen C. Jensen and Raymond E. Ivany were returned by search and not opened. One page each, outside careers stated.
